title: Candidate pattern: scoped resilience and cancellation ownership
summary: Assign retries, deadlines, circuit breaking, queueing, cooldowns, and cancellation to explicit scopes so nested layers do not multiply work or outlive the caller.
incompatible_when: The workload has no remote calls, concurrency, queueing, or cancellable operations.
procedure: Create a failure matrix covering caller, request, provider, connection, and process scopes.
Give each retry and timeout budget one owner and prevent blanket retries at multiple layers.
Propagate cancellation through queues, fallbacks, streams, and subprocess boundaries.
Bound concurrency and queue depth, and make overload behavior explicit.
Define recovery probes and success-decay behavior instead of relying only on timer expiry.
verification: Inject latency, cancellation, retryable failures, quota failures, and queue saturation and verify bounded work.
Confirm a disconnected caller cannot leave provider work, streams, or subprocesses running indefinitely.
rollback: Remove or specialize the lesson if a target runtime has incompatible cancellation or scheduling semantics.

confidence.rationale: OmniRoute documents scoped resilience and implements circuit-breaker/combo behavior, but cross-repository reuse is not yet proven.
